_purpose: GH-808 (queue item 3gy, part 1): the soil readings each case of tests/gh808-one-verdict-per-soil-element.test.js exports. Eight are live records of the stand, read verbatim from samples.payload; four are synthetic and say what they are for.
_source: docker exec gilba_mysql mysql -ugilba -pgilba_secret gilba -N --raw -e "SELECT id, payload FROM samples WHERE id IN (103,104,105,141,154,324,325,332)", read 2026-10-02. Read only: no row of the stand was written by this work.
_whyTheseEight: They are the records the defect was measured on, plus the records that make the other verdicts reachable. Each one says below what it is here for. The other 46 live soil records are not here: they are the same shapes with other numbers, and a case that adds nothing to the list of verdicts reached adds only runtime.
_heldConstant: The label, the sample date and the four non-reading constants (bulk density, depth, ESP, area) stay the fixture's own in every case -- see putSoilReadings in tests/helpers/export-page-sandbox.js for why: the date decides the staleness gate and the constants are in every ppm -> kg/ha conversion.
_site: Every case is exported as Test5 - NZ (Perennial Ryegrass, sand), so every case resolves the Hill Labs S277 certificate: P min 20 mg/L, K min 78.2 ppm, Ca min 400 ppm, Mg min 36.6 ppm, no S floor. A sample whose own site resolves S81 is NOT covered -- there is no S81 record on the stand, and the plan names that as a boundary of the measurement.
_tableBaselineIs: The rows the 'Annual Soil Amendments' table printed for each case BEFORE this work, in the document's own cell order: nutrient, soil deficit, programme delivers, residual, product, theoretical, practical, status. Measured 2026-10-02 by the run of tests/gh808-one-verdict-per-soil-element.test.js on the tree where assets/word-export.js was md5 bafee59b3a40b226207fceac00bc6089 (GH-803 in, GH-808 not yet). It is the POSITIVE CONTROL and the reason it is needed: the signs of this delivery are about what the report no longer says, and every one of them would go green if the table itself stopped printing. These rows are the only place a COMPUTED amendment rate appears, so they are pinned cell by cell -- the list, not its length. GH-821 changed one row by the owner's decision: synthetic-C has no pH, and its magnesium row printed kieserite chosen by a stand-in pH of 7.0; it now prints no product and says why, with the same deficit (23.2).

cases.what: Russley, Green 1, live. Ca 100 and Mg 21.87 are both far below the S277 floors, so this is the record whose table carries BOTH a gypsum row and an Epsom row -- the two amendments that the measured defect carried into another sample's Monthly Schedule.

Russley, Green 13, live. Ca 160 below the floor and Mg 36.45 just below it (36.6): its gypsum rate differs from 103's, which is how the second half of the defect shows -- two sections of ONE document naming two rates for one product.

Russley, Green 18, live, and the only live record with NO pH. Here for the pH substitution: today the decision substitutes 7.0 and prints a band chosen from a number the sample does not carry. Removing that substitution is part 2 of this work and is not asserted here -- this case records what the document says today.

Test5 - NZ, Soccer, live, and the fixture's OWN record. Here as the unchanged baseline: it is the sample every other suite exports, so a difference between its document here and there is a difference made by this case list rather than by the work.

Test - GC - NZ - warm season grass test, Main Oval, live. Every measured nutrient is at or above its floor, so its table says no standalone amendment is required -- which is why it is the receiving sample in the two-export case: whatever amendment its Monthly Schedule carries is not its own.

Hoxton Soccer - Kate's test, live, the client's own site. pH 5.3 with Ca below the floor: the record on which the report says in one paragraph that lime is NOT chosen and in the next to apply agricultural lime at 1-2 t/ha. Read only.

Hoxton Soccer - Kate's test, live, the later sample. This is the record the client quotes in R1 as '8.1:1 where the meq figure is 4.9:1' (541/67 = 8.07). Ca is above the floor and Mg is above it too, so no amendment row: it is here because the client's own numbers must not start printing an amendment.

Kate's test NZ - Christchurch, 18th Green, live. Ca 820 above the floor, Mg 95 above it, K 85 above it, and Na 45 at the top of its range: a record where the soil verdicts are all adequate and the sodium-saturation line of Cation Balance still fires.

cases.name: synthetic-A
cases.what: SYNTHETIC, from the plan. Ca 900 and Mg 45 with pH 6.2 and a CEC: Mg is ABOVE the S277 floor of 36.6, so the table says no amendment is required -- and Cation Balance, which uses its own floor of 50, says in the next paragraph that Mg sits below the sufficiency floor and recommends dolomite or kieserite. One element, two verdicts, on data that is not contradictory.

cases.name: synthetic-B
cases.what: SYNTHETIC, from the plan. Ca 900, Mg 30, pH 6.5: Mg is below the S277 floor but the gap is inside the marginal band, so the table and the Interpretation both say to monitor rather than amend -- while Cation Balance recommends dolomite or kieserite with a rate. A 'monitor' verdict and an 'apply' verdict on one element.

cases.name: synthetic-C
cases.what: SYNTHETIC, from the plan. Mg 20 below the floor and NO pH: today the decision substitutes pH 7.0 and the document prints 'Band: alkaline pH (7.0 >= 7.0). Kieserite chosen' -- a product chosen from a number the sample does not carry. The substitution is part 2 of this work; here this case carries the signs that hold whatever the words turn out to be. GH-821 removed it: no product is chosen without a pH, and the row says so.

cases.name: synthetic-D
cases.what: SYNTHETIC. K 30 against a floor of 78.2 -- a gap of 62 percent, so the deficit band is severe and the 'Severe K deficiency' line of Priority Actions fires. Here because that line is one of the seven places that decide an element today, and no live record on the stand reaches it: every live K is either above the floor or above half of it.

synthetic-C: pH was not reported on this sample, so the product is not chosen; deficit 23.2 kg Mg/ha
